title: The Unexpected Comeback of Film Photography
instructions: For questions 1-8, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap.
passage:
After decades (1)___ decline, film photography is, somewhat improbably, back in fashion. Sales of film stock, (2)___ once seemed destined for extinction, have risen for several years running, and prices for secondhand cameras have climbed (3)___ further, in some cases outstripping the cost of a new digital equivalent.

Much of the appeal lies (4)___ the unpredictability that digital photography was designed to eliminate: a roll of film cannot be checked, deleted or edited on the spot, (5)___ every shot forces the photographer to commit before they can see the result.

(6)___ this matters to a generation raised entirely on digital screens is less obvious than it might seem. Several young photographers interviewed for this piece said (7)___ enjoyed the discipline of a limited number of exposures, which (8)___ them think harder about composition before pressing the shutter.

questions.explanation: 'After decades of decline' uses 'of' to link a quantity expression ('decades') to the noun it describes ('decline').
A relative pronoun is needed to introduce a non-defining clause giving extra information about 'film stock' as the subject of 'seemed'.
'Even further' / 'still further' intensifies a comparison already established in the previous clause (sales rising, prices climbing).
'Lie in something' is a fixed verb + preposition pattern meaning 'to be found in' or 'consist of'.
'So' links the described limitation (film can't be checked or edited) to its consequence (every shot forces commitment).
A question word is needed to form the noun clause that acts as the subject of the sentence: 'Why this matters...is less obvious.'
A subject pronoun referring back to 'photographers' is needed before the verb 'enjoyed' in the reported clause.
The causative structure 'make someone do something' (bare infinitive, no 'to') fits 'which makes them think harder'.
